summary: Every farm problem has a fix, except running out of water. Thousands of farmers on Türkiye's Konya Plain pump from one shared aquifer, and NASA GRACE shows it has not recovered since 2021, while 704 sinkholes have opened. No single farmer can stop this; the decision has to be made for the whole region. Solo Medya SAC is a free web tool for DSİ (State Hydraulic Works, which sets each well's yearly water limit) and the Ministry of Agriculture (which plans to tie crop permits to basin crop patterns from 2027). It combines groundwater measured from space, crop water needs computed from NASA climate data, and the region's water allocation, and returns a well quota per decare and crop permits. Turning the satellite filter on in our example cuts the quota from 580 to 464 m³ per decare and keeps 11.6 million m³ of water in the ground every year.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Solo Medya SAC is a planning tool for water and agriculture authorities. A planner selects a region (Karapınar or Çumra in the prototype), enters the irrigated area and the water allocated today, and the tool returns:

- a groundwater alarm from NASA GRACE (red, yellow or green),

- each crop rotation's irrigation need per decare,

- a safe well quota per decare for DSİ's prepaid meter cards,

- how many decares of each crop the Ministry can permit,

- a side-by-side comparison of the decision without and with the satellite.

An AI planning assistant answers questions using only the data on the page.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Groundwater: the GRACE-based groundwater percentile (GRACEDADM CLSM 0.25°) sets the alarm. Below the 10th percentile is red, 10–30 is yellow. In 2025 the Konya Plain averaged the 1.5th percentile. GLDAS storage and SMAP soil moisture confirm the trend.

2. Crop water need: FAO-56 Penman–Monteith reference evapotranspiration from daily NASA POWER data (2001–2024: max/min temperature, humidity, wind, solar radiation), with SRTM elevation for air pressure. Crop coefficients turn it into crop water use; USDA-SCS effective rainfall is subtracted to get irrigation need.

3. Decision: the alarm level reduces the allocation (red −20%, yellow −10%; an adjustable starting setting). The tool then finds the largest area of the water-intensive rotation that still fits the safe budget.

RESULTS (Karapınar)

- Sugar beet–maize rotation: 746 mm/year; chickpea–barley: 450 mm/year (−40%).

- Example region of 100,000 decares and 58 million m³: quota falls from 580 to 464 m³/decare, beet–maize permits fall from 43,915 to 4,693 decares, and 11.6 million m³ stays in the ground each year.

- Validation: GPM IMERG and NASA POWER rainfall agree (r = 0.89); our crop water use runs 20–30% above local NİSAD values, so the saving is conservative.

WHY IT MATTERS

Groundwater depletion is global (California, Punjab, North China Plain, Tigris–Euphrates). The method uses only open global data, so any water authority can apply it with its own coordinates and crops.

LIMITS AND NEXT STEPS

Area values are examples; DSİ would enter real permit totals. Climate data is about 50 km resolution, and soil type and irrigation method are not yet included. Next: NISAR ground subsidence data, soil and irrigation inputs, and a pilot with real DSİ well data.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript, hosted on GitHub Pages (Turkish and English). The AI assistant uses Google Gemini through a Cloudflare Worker that keeps the API key private.
